system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

9.4.1.2.4 Page Parameter This parameter is coded as two 4-bit fields. The first field (bits 0-3) indicates the binary value of the total number of pages in the CBS message and the second field (bits 4-7) indicates binary the page number within that sequence. The coding starts at 0001, with 0000 reserved. If a mobile receives the code 0000 in either the first field or the second field then it shall treat the CBS message exactly the same as a CBS message with page parameter 0001 0001 (i.e. a single page message).

data.summary: The alert is not yet deliverable as drafted. There are three problems. The required Arabic version is missing. The English text runs to 3 pages, against UAE handset advice of 1 page. The text names the hazard but gives no protective action, so page 1 cannot carry both. The drafter can fix all three.

objections.issue: The UAE profile requires Arabic and English, but only an English phone text is provided. The Arabic version is missing.
objections.fix: Add an Arabic (ar) phone text with the same hazard, action, time and source. Arabic needs UCS-2 encoding, which allows only 70 characters per page, so write it short from the start.

evidence.quote: receiving and displaying emergency alerts in Arabic and English
Messages should support both English and Arabic languages.

objections.issue: The English text is 221 GSM-7 characters across 3 cell broadcast pages, but the UAE handset advice limits messages to 1 page. Each CBS page is a fixed 88 octets, so the text must be cut to fit one page.
objections.fix: Shorten the English text to fit one GSM-7 page (about 93 characters). Keep only the hazard, the area, the action and the end time. Move details such as the wind description and the source to a shorter form or a follow-up channel. Example: 'Dust/sand storm: visibility under 2km on coast & inland. Drive slowly, stay indoors. Until 19:00 4 Mar.' Do the same for the Arabic text within 70 UCS-2 characters.

evidence.quote: message should be limited to 1 page
the 88 octet fixed length CBS page

objections.issue: The text describes the hazard and its duration but contains no protective action, so the first page does not tell recipients what to do.
objections.fix: Put a clear action on the first page right after the hazard. For example, 'Avoid driving or drive slowly with headlights on; stay indoors if you have breathing problems.' Include the same action in the Arabic text.

evidence.quote: cutting visibility to under 2,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas
description of the threat and the protective action the public should take

no_basis.concern: I cannot confirm that the character count of 221 is consistent with the stated 3 pages and GSM-7 encoding. That depends on GSM-7 extension characters and the per-page limit of 93 characters, which none of the clauses shown states.
